question.text:
If $\mathrm{B}$ and $\mathrm{B}^{\prime}$ are the ends of minor axis and $\mathrm{S}$ and $\mathrm{S}^{\prime}$ are the foci of the ellipse $\frac{x^{2}}{25}+\frac{y^{2}}{9}=1$, then the area of the rhombus
$\mathrm{SBS}^{\prime} \mathrm{B}^{\prime}$ will be

solution.text: Hint: $\mathrm{B}=(0,3), \mathrm{B}^{\prime}=(0,-3)$ $\mathrm{S} \equiv(\mathrm{ae}, 0) \equiv\left(5 \times \sqrt{1-\frac{9}{25}}, 0\right) \equiv(4,0) \quad \therefore$ area $\mathrm{SBS}^{\prime} \mathrm{B}^{\prime}=2 \times$ area $\triangle \mathrm{BSB}^{\prime}=2 \times \frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 6=24$ sq. unit
